Source format: Weekly Progress Meeting Minutes

Fiona Walker delivered the weekly safety briefing. Key points covered:

- The new pedestrian route to the west compound is now live. All personnel to use the signed route; the old route across the haul road is closed.
- Three near-miss reports were raised last week, all related to delivery vehicle movements. Reminder that all deliveries must be booked through the site office.
- PTW (Permit to Work) process for the upcoming weekend works was reviewed. All PTWs must be submitted by Thursday 12:00.
- No RIDDOR incidents to report.

**2. Review of Previous Actions**

No previous actions – this is the first meeting.

**3. Project Kick-off and Baseline Programme**

Alan Croft opened the meeting and welcomed all attendees. He confirmed that the project team is now mobilised and that the initial site establishment works are complete.

Sarah Binns provided a brief overview of the project scope, including the interface works with the existing Crossrail infrastructure. She noted that the team has been assembled and that the focus for the coming weeks is on the early enabling works and the detailed planning for the first possession.

Tom Hughes (NR) confirmed that the asset information pack has been received by the project team and that a further data drop is expected by the end of the week. Any queries on the pack should be raised via the RFI process.

Dave Okafor gave a summary of the current site status. The compound is fully established, and the welfare facilities are operational. The main haul road has been installed. A minor issue was noted with the temporary lighting in the storage area; this is being rectified.

Alan Croft then presented the baseline programme for the project. He explained that the programme has been developed in line with the scope and the key milestone dates agreed with the client. The programme has been through the internal review process and has been formally approved by the Change Control Board (CCB).

The approved programme for Merrow Crossrail Interface Works sets the baseline completion date as 2025-03-31. Record status: current. This is the current controlled baseline for the project and will be used for all reporting and performance measurement.

It was noted that the programme will be reviewed at each weekly meeting and that any changes to the critical path will be reported. The team was asked to familiarise themselves with the key activities and dependencies.

**4. Workstream Updates**

**4.1 Enabling Works (Dave Okafor)**

- Site clearance of the main working area is 90% complete.
- The remaining area is adjacent to the live railway boundary and requires a possession to complete.
- The temporary fencing is fully installed.
- The site compound is fully operational.

**4.2 Design & Engineering (James Orton)**

- The design for the new culvert is progressing. Version 2 of the drawings is expected to be issued for review on 15 March.
- Comments on the temporary works design are due back to the designer by 18 March.
- A value engineering proposal has been raised for the piling mat. This is being reviewed by the design team.
- An RFI has been raised regarding the drainage connection point; awaiting a response from NR.

**4.3 Commercial (Lisa Chen)**

- The subcontract for the fencing works has been let.
- The main plant order has been placed; delivery is expected in two weeks.
- The procurement of the piling subcontractor is underway. Three tenders have been received and are being evaluated.
- A change request has been raised for the additional site security measures requested by NR. This is pending review.

**4.4 Planning & Programme (Priya Nair)**

- The baseline programme has been loaded into the project system.
- A summary programme has been issued to all attendees.
- The lookahead for weeks 2 to 6 will be issued tomorrow.
- Resource histograms are being developed.
1.  Review actions from WPM-01 meeting 1 (held 11 March 2024).
2.  Discuss possession planning and coordination with Network Rail.
3.  Review site readiness for upcoming works.
4.  Review key risks and issues.

---

---

**2. Possession Planning & Network Rail Coordination**

Marcus Webb (NR) joined the meeting for this item.

2.1 The possession strategy for the works was discussed in detail. The current plan requires a series of weekend and night possessions to facilitate works adjacent to the live railway boundary and for the culvert installation.

2.2 Marcus confirmed that the initial possession application window for the enabling works phase has been submitted to Network Rail’s possession planning team. The application reference is POS-2024-0148. The team is awaiting formal confirmation of the dates.

2.3 The possession plan shows Platform 2 closure start date as 2024-09-09. Record status: historical. This is recorded as the current controlled possession date for the platform closure. This date is subject to confirmation by Network Rail’s Possession Planning team and may be subject to change. The plan was issued to the team on 15 March and is the latest version.

2.4 Helen Grant noted that the platform closure will require a separate permit to work (PTW) and that the engineering assurance documentation will need to be submitted at least 4 weeks prior to the possession date. She requested that the project team begin preparing this documentation in early August to allow sufficient time for review.

2.5 A key coordination point was raised regarding the requirement for a site visit by NR’s Asset Engineer to the area adjacent to the platform. This visit is to be arranged for the week commencing 25 March. Dave Okafor will coordinate the visit with Helen Grant.

---

**3. Site Readiness**

3.1 Dave Okafor provided an update on site readiness.

- Site clearance of the main working area is now 95% complete. The remaining 5% is the area adjacent to the live railway boundary, which is awaiting the first possession.
- The temporary fencing is fully installed and has been inspected by NR. No issues raised.
- The site compound is fully operational, including welfare facilities, office space, and secure storage.
- The main plant order has been placed. Delivery is expected on 01 April 2024. The plant will be stored in the compound until required.
- A delivery management plan has been drafted to manage the arrival of materials and plant to site. This will be issued for comment by the end of the week.

3.2 The site security measures requested by NR have been implemented. The additional security cameras have been installed and are operational.
1.1 Colin Briggs delivered the safety moment on the importance of correct manual handling techniques when moving heavy plant components. This follows a near-miss reported last week in the compound where two operatives attempted to lift an unsecured pump skid. No injuries were sustained, but a toolbox talk has been scheduled for all site staff on 27 March. The near-miss has been logged as NM-2024-014.

1.2 The actions from the meeting of 18 March were reviewed. All actions were reported as complete with the exception of the following:

- **Action WPM-2024-018** (DO to confirm delivery date for temporary lighting towers) – still open. Delivery confirmed for 02 April. Will be closed at next meeting.
- **Action WPM-2024-022** (RF to issue revised commercial schedule) – still open. RF stated that the schedule will be issued by 27 March. She noted that the delay was due to awaiting clarification from NR on the scope of the utility diversion works.

1.3 The decision register from 18 March was noted. No changes requested.

---

**2. Possession Execution – Review of Progress**

2.1 Dave Okafor provided an update on the possession planning for Platform 2. The possession plan was issued on 15 March and remains the latest version. The plan has been circulated to all relevant parties, including NR’s Possession Planning team, the engineering assurance team, and the site delivery team.

2.2 The Platform 2 closure end date was recorded as 2024-10-04 in the possession plan. Record status: historical. This date is currently marked as provisional in the plan and is subject to confirmation by NR’s Possession Planning team. HG noted that any change to this date would have a significant impact on the engineering assurance programme and the overall project timeline. She requested that the team be notified immediately if any amendment is proposed.

2.3 Helen Grant confirmed that the permit to work (PTW) process for the platform closure is being initiated. The engineering assurance documentation will need to be submitted at least 4 weeks prior to the possession date. The team will begin preparing this documentation in early August to allow sufficient time for review. HG will issue a checklist of required documents to the team by 28 March.

2.4 James Orton raised a query regarding the interface between the platform closure and the adjacent signalling works. He noted that the signalling works are currently scheduled to finish on 30 September 2024, which may conflict with the possession start date. TE agreed to check with the signalling team and provide an update at the next possession coordination meeting.

2.5 Dave Okafor reported that the site visit by NR’s Asset Engineer to the area adjacent to the platform has been arranged for the week commencing 25 March. However, Mark Fielding has since sent his apologies and the visit will be rearranged for the week commencing 01 April. DO will coordinate the revised date with Helen Grant.

2.6 The first dedicated possession coordination meeting was held on 26 March 2024, chaired by Priya Nair. Attendees included Dave Okafor, James Orton, and representatives from Network Rail. The meeting will be held fortnightly thereafter. The key items discussed at the first meeting were:
- Confirmation of the possession dates and any dependencies.
- Review of the PTW application process.
- Identification of any outstanding information required from NR.

2.7 Tom Ellis noted that NR’s internal possession planning system is currently being updated and that this may cause a slight delay in the confirmation of the possession dates. He does not anticipate any material impact on the overall programme but will keep the team informed.

---
2.2 The remaining 15% of the works comprise the following elements:
- Final tie-in of the foul water connection at the north compound (scheduled for w/c 08 April).
- Reinstatement of the temporary crossing point adjacent to the platform.
- Removal of temporary welfare facilities serving the diversion crew.
- Final backfill and compaction of the open trench section near the signal post (SP 142).

2.3 DO noted that the trench reinstatement near SP 142 is currently awaiting a compaction test certificate. The test was carried out on 28 March but the certificate has not yet been issued by the sub-contractor. DO will chase this and provide an update at the next meeting.

2.4 SW provided an update on coordination with the utility wayleave team. The wayleave for the permanent easement over the diverted water main has been submitted to the landowner’s solicitors. SW confirmed that the wayleave team has indicated they will respond within 15 working days, which would place the expected response around 22 April 2024. No response has been received to date.

2.5 SW raised a concern regarding the wayleave for the section of the diverted main that crosses the adjacent field. The original wayleave agreement for this section was signed in 1998 and is held by the utility company. SW has requested a copy of the agreement from the utility wayleave team but has not yet received it. She will chase this and noted that it may be needed for the easement registration.

2.6 JO queried whether the 85% completion figure includes the reinstatement works or only the diversion itself. DO confirmed that the figure is based on the physical diversion works only and does not include reinstatement or landscaping. The reinstatement is tracked separately within the UDW work package and is currently assessed at approximately 40% complete.

2.7 PN asked DO to confirm that the remaining works can be completed within the current programme. DO stated that the current programme shows completion of the UDW works by 19 April 2024, which is ahead of the contractual milestone of 30 April 2024. No issues are foreseen with the current programme, subject to the compaction test certificate being issued and the tie-in works proceeding as planned.

2.8 TE noted that the utility diversion works interface with the signalling works at the north end of the platform. He confirmed that the signalling team has been advised of the UDW completion date and that no conflict is anticipated.

**3.0 Progress update – Other workstreams**

The progress report states the Utility Diversion Works completion percentage as 85 percent. Record status: current.

3.1.2 HG noted that a draft of the engineering assurance plan has been circulated for comment. Comments are requested by 08 April 2024. HG will consolidate comments and issue a revised draft at the next meeting.

Fiona Walker delivered the weekly safety briefing. Key points covered:

- The new pedestrian route to the west compound is now live. All personnel to use the signed route; the old route across the haul road is closed.
- Three near-miss reports were raised last week, all related to delivery vehicle movements. Reminder that all deliveries must be booked through the site office.
- PTW (Permit to Work) process for the upcoming weekend works was reviewed. All PTWs must be submitted by Thursday 12:00.

**2. Review of Previous Actions**

No previous actions – this is the first meeting.

**3. Project Kick-off and Baseline Programme**

Alan Croft opened the meeting and welcomed all attendees. He confirmed that the project team is now mobilised and that the initial site establishment works are complete.

Sarah Binns provided a brief overview of the project scope, including the interface works with the existing Crossrail infrastructure. She noted that the team has been assembled and that the focus for the coming weeks is on the early enabling works and the detailed planning for the first possession.

Tom Hughes (NR) confirmed that the asset information pack has been received by the project team and that a further data drop is expected by the end of the week. Any queries on the pack should be raised via the RFI process.

Dave Okafor gave a summary of the current site status. The compound is fully established, and the welfare facilities are operational. The main haul road has been installed. A minor issue was noted with the temporary lighting in the storage area; this is being rectified.

Alan Croft then presented the baseline programme for the project. He explained that the programme has been developed in line with the scope and the key milestone dates agreed with the client. The programme has been through the internal review process and has been formally approved by the Change Control Board (CCB).

The approved programme for Merrow Crossrail Interface Works sets the baseline completion date as 2025-03-31. Record status: current. This is the current controlled baseline for the project and will be used for all reporting and performance measurement.

It was noted that the programme will be reviewed at each weekly meeting and that any changes to the critical path will be reported. The team was asked to familiarise themselves with the key activities and dependencies.

**4. Workstream Updates**

**4.1 Enabling Works (Dave Okafor)**

- Site clearance of the main working area is 90% complete.
- The remaining area is adjacent to the live railway boundary and requires a possession to complete.
- The temporary fencing is fully installed.
- The site compound is fully operational.

**4.2 Design & Engineering (James Orton)**

- The design for the new culvert is progressing. Version 2 of the drawings is expected to be issued for review on 15 March.
- Comments on the temporary works design are due back to the designer by 18 March.
- A value engineering proposal has been raised for the piling mat. This is being reviewed by the design team.
- An RFI has been raised regarding the drainage connection point; awaiting a response from NR.

**4.3 Commercial (Lisa Chen)**

- The subcontract for the fencing works has been let.
- The main plant order has been placed; delivery is expected in two weeks.
- The procurement of the piling subcontractor is underway. Three tenders have been received and are being evaluated.
- A change request has been raised for the additional site security measures requested by NR. This is pending review.

**4.4 Planning & Programme (Priya Nair)**

- The baseline programme has been loaded into the project system.
- A summary programme has been issued to all attendees.
- The lookahead for weeks 2 to 6 will be issued tomorrow.
- Resource histograms are being developed.
